questions.stem: Sales representatives must see only their own region's rows in a warehouse table. What do you build?

options.text: Dynamic data masking on the Region column
A view per region, shared by email
A deployment rule
A security policy that applies an inline table-valued function as a filter predicate

questions.explanation: Row-level security uses a predicate function and a security policy, so every query on the table returns only the rows the predicate allows for the user.

questions.stem: Analysts may query a Patients table but must never read its Diagnosis column. Which T-SQL statement implements column-level security?

options.text: CREATE SECURITY POLICY ON dbo.Patients
GRANT UNMASK TO Analysts
ALTER TABLE dbo.Patients DROP COLUMN Diagnosis
GRANT SELECT ON dbo.Patients (PatientID, Name, City) TO Analysts

questions.explanation: Granting SELECT on a list of columns lets the role read those columns only. A query that touches Diagnosis fails for them.

questions.stem: A reporting role must never read the dbo.StagingOrders table. Which statement implements object-level security?

options.text: DENY SELECT ON dbo.StagingOrders TO ReportingRole
CREATE SECURITY POLICY ReportingRole
ALTER TABLE dbo.StagingOrders DROP COLUMN ReportingRole
GRANT SELECT ON dbo.StagingOrders TO ReportingRole

questions.explanation: Object-level security controls access to whole objects such as tables and views with GRANT, REVOKE and DENY.

questions.stem: Users may read some folders in a lakehouse's Files section but not others. What controls access at folder level?

options.text: OneLake security roles that grant access to specific folders and tables
Dynamic data masking
Deployment rules
Sensitivity labels

questions.explanation: OneLake security lets you define roles over specific tables and folders, so access to data is granted below the item level.

questions.stem: A warehouse table has a row-level security policy that shows each rep only their own rows. Workspace Contributors need to see every row to validate the data. What do you do?

options.text: Write the security policy's predicate so that it also allows those users
Turn the policy off for their sessions with STATE = OFF
Nothing; Contributors are exempt from row-level security
Grant them UNMASK on the table

questions.explanation: Security policies apply to all users, including dbo and table owners. If some people must see all rows, the predicate has to allow them.

questions.stem: A Sales table has a row-level security policy. A new SalesArchive table holds the same columns but has no policy. What do users see when they query SalesArchive?

options.text: No rows until a policy is created
Only their own rows, because the Sales policy applies to similar tables
All rows, because each table needs its own policy
Only rows older than a year

questions.explanation: Row-level security is defined per table. A table without a policy returns unfiltered data.

questions.stem: A security officer must create a security policy in a warehouse schema. Which two permissions does creating the policy itself require? Each correct answer is part of the solution.

options.text: CONTROL on the capacity
UNMASK
ALTER permission on the schema
ALTER ANY SECURITY POLICY
ALTER ANY MASK

questions.explanation: Creating a security policy needs ALTER ANY SECURITY POLICY and ALTER on the schema, plus SELECT and REFERENCES on the predicate objects. UNMASK and ALTER ANY MASK are masking permissions.

questions.stem: Charlie was granted SELECT on every column of dbo.Customers except CreditCard. What happens when he runs SELECT * FROM dbo.Customers?

options.text: The query fails with a SELECT permission denied error on the CreditCard column
The query returns all columns, with CreditCard shown as NULL
The query returns only the columns he was granted
The query returns CreditCard masked as XXXX

questions.explanation: Column-level security doesn't silently drop columns. Any query that includes the denied column, such as SELECT *, fails.

questions.stem: A user belongs to two OneLake security roles on a lakehouse table. One role's row filter allows Region = 'East', the other allows Region = 'West'. Which rows does the user see?

options.text: Only East rows, from the first role created
All rows, because multiple roles cancel row filters
No rows, because the filters conflict
Rows for both East and West

questions.explanation: OneLake combines roles as a union. When several roles grant the same table, their row-level rules combine with OR.

questions.stem: OneLake security is enabled on a lakehouse. An admin deletes the DefaultReader role. What happens to users who have only the ReadAll permission?

options.text: They get write access instead
They lose data access until they're added to another role that grants it
They keep access, because ReadAll grants data access on its own
Nothing changes until the lakehouse is redeployed

questions.explanation: With OneLake security on, ReadAll grants data access only through DefaultReader. Workspace Admins, Members and Contributors keep access through their Write permission.
